envy verb

also how I envy you, I envy you, be envious of, begrudge, jealous, jealousy, envious, be jealous of

classical

Cic. Flacc. 70: tibi invideō, quod ūnīs vestīmentīs tam diū lautus es (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 134
Cic. Fl. 70: in quā tibi invideō (Lewis & Short)
Verg. Ecl. 1.11: nōn equidem invideō; mīror magis
Traupman 22: Tibi quidem invideō.
Traupman 152, 155
Traupman 310

invideō, invidēre, invīdī, invīsum

verb, second conjugation, with the dative of the person

envy, begrudge

Latin envies to someone: tibi invideō, I envy you; what one envies goes in a quod-clause, or in the ablative with in.

Other words

  • invidia, invidiae f. — envy, jealousy (the feeling)

    noun, first declension · classical · Caes. BG 1.7: invidia atque obtrectātiō laudis suae (Lewis & Short); Cic. Tusc. 3.20 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 152, 155; Traupman 310

    Both the envy one feels and the ill will one suffers (Cic. Tusc. 4.16, Lewis & Short).

  • invidus, invida, invidum — envious, jealous

    also used · classical · Cic. Mur. 20 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 152, 155; Traupman 310

Examples

  • Quam tibi invideō!

    How I envy you!Traupman 134

  • nōn equidem invideō; mīror magis

    I don’t envy you; rather, I wonderVerg. Ecl. 1.11

See also rather.
